claims.text: Catalytic activity of transition-metal catalysts is governed by the position of the d-band center relative to the Fermi level.
Catalytic selectivity of transition-metal catalysts is governed by the position of the d-band center relative to the Fermi level.
Catalyst durability is governed by the position of the d-band center relative to the Fermi level.
Alloying a pure transition-metal catalyst with a second transition metal can shift its d-band center.
The alloying-induced shift of the d-band center tunes the adsorption energies of key reaction intermediates.
Shifting the d-band center changes the binding strength of reaction intermediates.
Excessively strong intermediate binding can poison a catalyst.
Intermediate binding that is too weak can hinder activation.
An optimally positioned d-band center produces intermediate adsorption energies that are neither too strong nor too weak.
An alloyed catalyst with an optimally shifted d-band center will have a higher turnover frequency than the pure-metal baseline.
An alloyed catalyst with an optimally shifted d-band center will give a higher yield of the desired product than the pure-metal baseline.
An alloyed catalyst with an optimally shifted d-band center will degrade less during cycling than the pure-metal baseline.
The proposed mechanism should apply when adsorption of intermediates is rate-limiting and primarily controlled by electronic structure.
Changes in particle morphology, surface oxidation state, and support interactions can independently affect reaction kinetics.
XPS or UPS can be used to characterize d-band-center positions in the proposed catalyst series.
A lack of correlation between measured d-band-center position and catalytic performance would falsify the proposed governing relationship.
